newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's hard left sees "storm clouds" over Eurotax.
newsitem.headline: Italy's hard left sees "storm clouds" over Eurotax.

text.p: Italy's hardline Communist Refoundation party on Wednesday rejected proposals by the small centrist Italian Renewal party for changes to a controversial "Euro-tax" planned as part of the tough 1997 budget.
Oliviero Diliberto, party leader in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), slammed alternative proposals unveiled by Italian Renewal as "indecent" and warned: "Storm clouds are gathering."
Dini's party is a member of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government. Prodi relies on Communist Refoundation for a majority in the lower house.
"The proposal to make pensioners pay the Euro-tax is quite simply indecent," Diliberto told reporters, adding that extra spending cuts would destroy Italy's welfare state.
"I see storm clouds on the horizon," he added. "I ask Prime Minister Prodi...to make his voice heard."
The Euro-tax aims to raise 12.5 trillion lire ($8.26 billion) to help get Italy in shape to become a founder member of a European single currency due for launch in 1999.
It is a key element of Prodi's 1997 austerity budget, which is designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit.

Communist Refoundation's support helped the government get the budget through the Chamber, where opposition parties staged a boycott. But the Euro-tax was not part of discussions during the budget's parliamentary passage in the lower house.
Opposition from Communist Refoundation could, however, hurt the government's prospects of finally approving the Euro-tax.
Italian Renewal's proposals included imposing a corporate tax instead of a planned levy on severance pay and a one-off charge on early retirement pensions.
It also suggested modifications to the planned method of collecting the tax via a hike in income tax.

Cesare Salvi, leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) in the Senate (upper house), told reporters earlier that the government planned to unveil changes of its own to the Euro-tax at 1900 GMT. The PDS is the biggest party in Prodi's government. ($1=1514 Lire)
